holidays.name: National Leprechaun Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace Irish folklore's mischievous little shoemaker. Hunt for rainbows, hide gold chocolate coins around the house, wear green, and keep a sharp eye out for tiny tricksters. Just don't take your eyes off one, or he'll vanish.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It gives fans of Irish folklore a second chance to celebrate leprechauns outside St. Patrick's Day.
holidays.funFact: In Irish folklore, a captured leprechaun must grant you his hidden pot of gold, but he's famous for tricking his captor into looking away so he can escape.

holidays.name: Frog Jumping Day
holidays.description: A day for hopping, leaping, and cheering on amphibian athletes. Hold a leap-frog race, make paper frogs and see whose jumps farthest, or just croak out a salute to the world's most spring-loaded critter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's often linked to the jumping frog contest tradition made famous by Mark Twain's tall tale about a gambling frog in Calaveras County, California.
holidays.funFact: The Calaveras County Jumping Frog Jubilee, inspired by Twain's story, has a record-setting jump of 21 feet 5¾ inches by a frog named Rosie the Ribeiter in 1986.
